newsitem.title: USA: Delay of U.S. arms for Bosnia costs $50,000 daily.
newsitem.headline: Delay of U.S. arms for Bosnia costs $50,000 daily.

text.p: Delay in delivering a consignment of U.S. arms to Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation, held up until Sarajevo fires a minister Washington dislikes, is costing nearly $50,000 per day, the State Department said on Tuesday.

State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said the huge cost of having a ship stand off the Aegean port of Ploce waiting to unload the arms prompted questions about how long the United States would continue the wait.

"It's costing many tens of thousands of dollars, close to $50,000 a day, to keep that ship off of Ploce, which then raises an issue of, you know, how long one can sustain that," Davies told a news conference in answer to a question.
Washington is delaying delivery of the weaponry until Sarajevo fires Deputy Defence Minister Hasan Cengic, whom Washington considers too close to Iran.
Davies added: "Our expectation is that Sarajevo will come through on this one, and that we'll be able to put the ship into port and offload the equipment."
Davies said the extra expense was "still within the monies appropriated for the purpose of obtaining the equipment and getting there."
The ship carrying the $100 million of weaponry, including tanks and helicopters, arrived at the Croatian port on October 24 for transporting across land to Bosnia.

It is part of a U.S. "Train and Equip" programme combining military hardware and instruction for federation army troops, devised to ensure parity of forces in the region and help the federation army counter any future threat from its Serb foes.

The Moslem-led Bosnian army was outgunned by Serb forces during the 43-month war and had to rely on Islamic countries such as Iran for arms shipments, which violated an international arms embargo on former Yugoslavia.
